sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Like *én*, the word *mi* (“we”) is usually left out: say *Tanulunk.*, not *Mi tanulunk.* Say *mi* only when you mean “we, not they”. You already know *mi* as “what” (*Mi ez?*). Here it is a second word with the same spelling, and the verb ending *-unk/-ünk* tells you which one you are reading.

sections.title: Anna and I
sections.content: When you name someone together with yourself, the verb takes the “we” ending: *Anna és én olvasunk.* means “Anna and I read.” The speaker is one of the people, so it is a “we” sentence.

sections.title: Without and with mi
rows: We are the ones who read.

items.english: We are the ones who cook.

items.spanish: Meg és én a kertben sétálunk.
items.english: Meg and I walk in the garden.

sections.content: Keep *mi* for contrast. If every sentence starts with *mi*, it sounds as if you were stressing “we” each time.
